title: Stop switching AI tools. Do these 3 things instead.
hook: Stop switching AI tools. Do these 3 things instead.

body: Metricool: scheduled Thu 22 Oct 13:00 IG + TikTok

Motion slides (7 x 8 s loops, 1080x1350):
1. Stop switching AI tools. Do these 3 things instead. (Masked type)
2. Every switch is day one
3. Pick one. 30 days.
4. Hand off what you hate
5. Talk to it like a colleague
6. Save the context prompt
7. Want my 30-day AI starter plan? Comment START (CTA)
guide: The post argues you should stop hopping between AI tools and instead commit to one for 30 days. You need one AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude or similar), a notes app such as Notion, and a few minutes a day.
1. Pick one assistant, such as ChatGPT or Claude, and write down the date you start.
1. Commit to using only that tool for 30 days, and ignore new launches until the 30 days are up.
1. List the tasks you dislike doing (drafting emails, summarising notes, tidying spreadsheets) and hand one of them to the assistant each day.
1. Talk to it as you would a colleague: say what you want, why you want it and who it is for, then reply with corrections instead of starting again.
1. Once a conversation produces a good result, ask the assistant to write a short context prompt covering your role, your audience and your preferred tone.
1. Save that prompt in Notion, or any notes app, and paste it at the start of future chats so you never begin from zero.
1. At day 30, review which tasks you handed off and decide whether to stay or switch with evidence.
Watch out: every time you switch tools you start again from day one, losing the habits and context you built, so do not switch before the 30 days are done.

```
You are my AI onboarding coach. I want to commit to a single AI assistant, <ChatGPT / Claude / other>, for 30 days instead of switching tools.
About me: I work as <your role> and my audience is <who you write or work for>. The tasks I dislike most are <task 1>, <task 2> and <task 3>.
Build me a 30-day starter plan that:
- gives me one small task to hand off each day, drawn from my list and getting gradually harder
- shows me how to brief you like a colleague: the goal, the audience, the format and an example of good work
- includes a reusable context prompt, written in the first person, that holds my role, audience, tone and rules, which I can paste at the start of any new chat
- has a short review on day 30 so I can judge what saved me time
Keep the plan in plain English, with no jargon. Return a day-by-day table, then the context prompt on its own, ready to copy into <Notion / my notes app>. Ask me up to five questions first if you need more detail.
```
